graders.name: b1-sql-injection
graders.evidence:
This PR shouldn't be merged yet: I found 6 confirmed defects, 5 of them high severity. Search on `/api/books/search` is unreachable, the author match is built by pasting user input into the SQL, and the HTML results echo the query unescaped. Several of the new tests would also fail against this code, so the "`npm run test:run` passes" criterion isn't met. This comes from reading the code; I didn't run the test suite.

```json
[
  {
    "file": "src/models/book.ts",
    "line": 52,
    "severity": "high",
    "issue": "The author clause builds SQL by pasting user input into the query string instead of using a parameter. The search text is inserted as `author LIKE '${pattern}'`, and only the title placeholder gets a bound value. The escaping handles \\, % and _ but not quotes, so a query with an apostrophe breaks the statement and a crafted query can inject SQL. This violates 'SQL is parameterised: no string-built queries'.",
    "evidence": "Line 52: `... OR author LIKE '${pattern}' ESCAPE '\\\\' ...`; line 53 binds only `[pattern]`. 'Ender's' becomes `author LIKE '%Ender's%'`, which is a syntax error; \"x' OR 1=1 --\" is injected. The apostrophe test and the AC4 injection tests exercise exactly these inputs."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/models/book.ts",
    "line": 37,
    "severity": "high",
    "issue": "Off-by-one in the length check: `>=` rejects a trimmed query of exactly 100 characters, but only queries over 100 should be rejected.",
    "evidence": "`if (trimmed.length >= MAX_SEARCH_QUERY_LENGTH)` with the limit set to 100. The 'exactly 100 characters is allowed' tests in the model, API and HTML test files all expect it to be accepted."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/routes/api.ts",
    "line": 40,
    "severity": "high",
    "issue": "`/books/search` is registered after `/books/:id`, so Express treats 'search' as a book id. The search endpoint always returns 404 'Book not found'; only the `/api/books?q=` alias works.",
    "evidence": "`router.get('/books/:id', ...)` is at line 29 and `router.get('/books/search', searchHandler)` at line 40. `parseInt('search')` is NaN, so no book is found. Every `/api/books/search` test in book-search.api.test.ts would get a 404."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/routes/books.ts",
    "line": 15,
    "severity": "high",
    "issue": "On the HTML endpoint, an empty or whitespace-only query shows no books instead of all books, which breaks the 'empty query returns all books' criterion.",
    "evidence": "`const books = query ? Book.searchBooks(query) : [];` renders 'No books found matching \"\"'. The HTML tests for no q, `q=` and a whitespace-only q expect all 50 cards."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/views/books/search-results.ejs",
    "line": 2,
    "severity": "high",
    "issue": "Reflected XSS: the user's query is written into the page unescaped with `<%- query %>`.",
    "evidence": "`No books found matching \"<%- query %>\"`. With q=<script>alert(1)</script> and no match, the raw script tag is sent back. The HTML test expects `<script>`. Use `<%= query %>` instead."
  },
  {
    "file": "tests/search/book-search.model.test.ts",
    "line": 62,
    "severity": "low",
    "issue": "The case-insensitive author test only checks `Array.isArray(...)`, which is always true. It can't fail, so author case-insensitivity isn't actually tested.",
    "evidence": "`expect(Array.isArray(Book.searchBooks(q))).toBe(true);` for ['FRANK HERBERT', 'frank herbert', 'fRaNk HeRbErT']. The title test just above it correctly asserts `toEqual(['Dune'])`."
  }
]
```

| Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| high | `src/models/book.ts:52` | Author clause pastes user input into the SQL (injection; apostrophes cause a 500) |
| high | `src/models/book.ts:37` | `>=` rejects exactly 100 characters |
| high | `src/routes/api.ts:40` | `/books/search` is caught by `/books/:id`, so it always returns 404 |
| high | `src/routes/books.ts:15` | An empty query on the HTML endpoint returns no books instead of all |
| high | `src/views/books/search-results.ejs:2` | Reflected XSS through unescaped `<%- query %>` |
| low | `tests/search/book-search.model.test.ts:62` | Author case-insensitivity test can't fail |

Reviewed 9 files against the BOOK-101 ticket: 6 findings (9 candidates; 1 dropped as unproven, 2 duplicates merged).

The dropped candidate: htmx doesn't display 400 responses by default, so a user typing over 100 characters might see no error message. It wasn't kept because it doesn't break any acceptance criterion, and the existing review route already returns errors the same way.

Reviewed 11 files against SPEC.md: 0 findings (1 candidate, 1 dropped by the verifier).

**The dropped candidate:** `src/routes/books.ts:19` returns the 400 error fragment for queries over 100 characters, but the page's bundled htmx (version 1.9.12) doesn't swap error responses into the page by default. So in the browser, the "Search query must be 100 characters or fewer" message never appears and the old results stay on screen. It was dropped because SPEC.md asks for exactly that 400 response, and neither the ticket nor the spec says the message has to be visible. If you want users to see it, the spec needs changing: either return the error with a 200, or add htmx handling for 400 responses.

What checked out:
- Every query is parameterised, and `%`, `_` and `\` in user input are escaped so they match literally.
- The results template escapes all values.
- The search route is registered before `/books/:id`, and `GET /api/books` only acts as a search when `q` is present.
- Input is trimmed before the 100-character check.
- The test expectations match the seed data.

I didn't run `npm run test:run` or the type check, so whether the tests pass is still unconfirmed.

${err.message}

`)`. The search box in src/views/books/index.ejs uses `hx-get=\"/books/search\" hx-target=\"#search-results\"` with the bundled htmx.org ^1.9.12. I checked this by reading the code; I couldn't run `npm run test:run` or `npx tsc --noEmit` because I have no shell here. Run both before merging.

What I checked against `TICKET.md` and `SPEC.md`:

- **Model (`src/models/book.ts`):** `normalizeSearchQuery` follows the spec. Missing or null input becomes `''`. Anything that isn't a string gives the "must be a string" error. Input is trimmed before the length check, 100 characters is allowed and 101 is rejected, and the error messages match the spec exactly.
- **SQL safety:** `searchBooks` escapes `\`, `%` and `_` before searching. The JavaScript string `"... ESCAPE '\\' ..."` reaches SQLite as `ESCAPE '\'`, which is correct, and the query uses `?` parameters only. An empty query returns `getAllBooks()`, so the ordering is the same.
- **JSON API (`src/routes/api.ts`):** `/books/search` is registered before `/books/:id`. The `?q=` alias only kicks in when `q` is present, so `GET /api/books` without it works as before. Errors return 400 with `{ error }`. Running the query through `normalizeSearchQuery` twice is harmless because trimming twice gives the same result.
- **HTML route and view:** `src/routes/books.ts` renders the new fragment, which uses the same card markup as `books/index.ejs`. All values are escaped with `<%= %>`, so the XSS tests are covered. The error branch puts `err.message` straight into the HTML, but it's always one of two fixed messages, never user input.
- **Tests:** I checked every expected result against `seed.sql`, for example "martin" returning four books, "Hunt", "le guin", "andy weir" in title order, and the wildcard and injection queries returning nothing. They all match. Each test file uses its own database in the system temp folder, following the conventions in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Constraints:** The diff doesn't touch `schema.sql`, `seed.sql`, `package.json`, `.env` or `bookshelf.db`.

One thing outside the diff, so I didn't count it as a defect: `bookshelf.db-shm` and `bookshelf.db-wal` are sitting in the working tree, and `.gitignore` only ignores `*.db`. Make sure those two files don't get committed by accident.
